title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Section 4 of the notes builds, for each MD-graph (stable graph) G of numerical type (g,ν), a 'multiplicité' (stack) M̂_G = ∏_{α∈S} M̂_{g_α, Î_α}, a product of Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactified moduli stacks over Spec Z. The previous page defines a clutching morphism (36) M̂_G → M̂_{g,I}. It takes a family of stable marked curves (Y_α) and glues the points labelled by the half-edges Ã in pairs via σ_Ã. That page notes (36) is a local immersion (unramified) but not an immersion. It is Γ = Aut G-equivariant, with Γ acting on M̂_{g,I} through Γ → S_I.

This page passes to quotient stacks. Set M̂_[G] := [M̂_G/Γ] and M̂_{g,ν} ≃ [M̂_{g,I}/S_I]. The equivariant map then induces a canonical morphism (37) M̂_[G] → M̂_{g,ν}.

Grothendieck claims (37) is a closed immersion of stacks proper and smooth over Z. Consequences he draws:
- The closure of the open stratum M_[G] (curves whose dual graph is exactly G) in M̂_{g,ν} is explicitly a proper smooth substack over Spec Z. He finds this 'a priori mysterious!'.
- The specializations [G'] of [G] are exactly the types occurring in M̂_G. Equivalently, a stratification of M̂_G = ∏ M̂_{g_α,Î_α} is given by choosing a stable graph with legs Î_α at each vertex α. This is the standard description of degenerations of a stable graph by blowing up vertices, inverse to edge contraction.

The next page (§5, 'Spécialisation des MD-graphes') develops this second point.

In modern terms: the gluing map ξ_G: ∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v} → M̄_{g,n} and its factorization through [∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v}/Aut G]. The goal is to describe boundary strata closures and the specialization order on stable graphs, as input for the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}.
errors: The claim that (37) is a (closed) immersion is false in general. The map [∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v}/Aut G] → M̄_{g,n} is finite and unramified, and an isomorphism over the open stratum M_[G]. It is not a monomorphism wherever the closure of the stratum self-intersects. Example: G = one vertex of genus g−1 with one loop. M̂_[G] = [M̄_{g−1,2}/S_2] maps 2:1 onto the locus of curves with two non-separating nodes, since one may normalize either node to get distinct objects of M̂_[G]. Correct statement: M̂_[G] is the normalization of the closure of M_[G]. That closure is in general only a normal-crossings substack, not smooth; e.g. the boundary divisor Δ_irr is not smooth. So the 'mysterious' smoothness of the closure does not hold.

The marginal note on the previous page ('imm. locale, mais pas une immersion [il se factorise par ... Γ = Aut G]') diagnoses non-injectivity only as coming from Aut G. The further non-injectivity, from different graph-strata of M̂_G mapping to the same stratum of M̂_{g,ν}, is overlooked here.

ideas.what: Gluing/clutching morphism from the product of moduli stacks attached to the vertices of a stable graph, made Aut(G)-equivariant and descended to the quotient stack [M̂_G/Aut G] → M̂_{g,ν}.
ideas.modern_name: clutching/gluing map ξ_G : M̄_G = ∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v} → M̄_{g,n}, and M̄_G/Aut(G) as normalization of the boundary stratum closure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983, clutching morphisms); Deligne–Mumford 1969; standard in Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths, Graber–Pandharipande
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν} and its stratification qualitatively; no explicit statement known

ideas.what: Specializations of a stable graph G correspond to strata of ∏ M̂_{g_α,Î_α}, i.e. to choosing a stable graph with legs Î_α at each vertex.
ideas.modern_name: degeneration (inverse edge-contraction) order on stable graphs; stratification of M̄_{g,n} by dual graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore since Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen; Arbarello–Cornalba, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads)

ideas.what: Moduli multiplicities M̂_{g,ν} as proper smooth stacks over Spec Z, presented as quotients [M̂_{g,I}/S_I].
ideas.modern_name: M̄_{g,n} as a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z; unordered marked points as an S_n-quotient

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material on boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} via clutching maps and graph specialization. The only distinctive feature is an erroneous claim (closed immersion, smooth closure), not an overlooked result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'On en déduit donc un morphisme cano-[nique]' continuing on the next line 'de multiplicités schématiques'.

The deleted/inserted passage after 'Spec Z — qui' appears to read 'qui [-paraît-] paraîtrait a priori mystérieux !'. The word written in the margin and underlined/encircled above 'mystérieux' looks like 'a priori'.
'[-comme-] sous-multiplicité': the struck word is 'comme', followed by 'sous-multipl[icité]'.
The underlined word 'immersion' is written over an earlier attempt (overwritten letters 'imm...').
